LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a standard AUR .SRCINFO metadata file for the basctl package. It contains package metadata (description, version, dependencies, sources, checksums) typical of Arch User Repository packaging. The sources include a git repository from the project's own GitHub (github.com/beangle/basctl) tagged at v0.0.1, plus sysusers and tmpfiles configuration files. The sha256sums field includes 'SKIP' for the VCS source, which is required and standard practice for VCS-based AUR packages, along with two additional hashes for the other sources. There are no obfuscated commands, no eval/base64/curl|bash patterns, no unexpected network destinations, and no code execution logic within this metadata file itself. All dependencies listed (bash, curl, logrotate, openssl, zlib) are standard system utilities and libraries. No evidence of injected malicious code, data exfiltration, or backdoor behavior was found.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for basctl.install:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard Arch Linux `.install` script for the `basctl` package. The hooks (`post_install`, `post_upgrade`, `pre_remove`, `post_remove`) create a system user/group (`bas`/`beangle`), set up directories under `/var/lib/bas` and `/var/log/bas`, install a config file only if missing, manage symlinks, and reload/enable/disable the `basagent.service` systemd unit. All operations are confined to package-owned paths and standard systemd service management. There are no network requests, no code downloads, no obfuscation, no `eval`/`base64`/`curl`/`wget`, and no data exfiltration. The script follows conventional AUR packaging practices for system service installation.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard Arch Linux packaging file for the basctl package. It clones the upstream Git repository at a tagged version, builds the D language project using dub, and installs binaries and configuration files to expected system locations. All commands are explicit and visible: no obfuscation, no encoded payloads, no execution of arbitrary downloaded scripts, and no modification of files outside the package's scope. The use of dub fetch is normal for D projects, and the SKIP checksum on the VCS source is standard practice. The backup directive for /etc/logrotate.d/bas is routine for packages managing logrotate configs. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, backdoors, or any other malicious behavior.
</details>
